summary: Verified the mobile overscroll/rubber-band fix on /demo-trade. On iPhone-emulated viewport (390x844, hover=none, pointer=coarse, touch enabled) the DemoTrade useEffect correctly sets document.body/documentElement inline overscrollBehavior='none' + overflow='hidden' at mount, and the root div carries 'overflow-hidden overscroll-none touch-pan-x' plus inline overscrollBehavior:'none'. Aggressive synthetic touch drags (pull-down from top ~400px, pull-down from chart middle ~500px, pull-up from bottom trade panel) produced ZERO vertical scroll offset, zero body/root shift, and root.bottom == window.innerHeight (no extra strip). Navigating away to '/' cleanly restored html/body inline overscroll/overflow to their original empty values (cleanup works). Desktop 1440x900 regression: chart canvas, header, side rail, asset tabs, trade panel all render correctly; overscroll lock is applied while on /demo-trade and restored on navigation away.

mobile_390x844_touch_emulated.cdp_features: Emulation.setEmulatedMedia hover=none pointer=coarse + Emulation.setTouchEmulationEnabled=true applied BEFORE /demo-trade navigation
mobile_390x844_touch_emulated.root_div_classes: h-[100dvh] flex flex-col text-white bg-[#040D09] overflow-hidden overscroll-none touch-pan-x

after_aggressive_touch_drags.verdict: No rubber-band strip visible at top or bottom; root fills viewport exactly.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix is minimal and correctly scoped: single useEffect in DemoTrade.jsx snapshots prior inline values and restores them in cleanup, so no leakage to other routes. Uses inline styles rather than a class on body — good, as it avoids conflicts with any global body class rules.

Belt-and-braces: root div also has Tailwind 'overscroll-none' + inline overscrollBehavior:'none' + 'touch-pan-x' (allows horizontal but blocks vertical browser gestures). Combined with html/body overflow:hidden this fully suppresses pull-to-refresh/rubber-band on WebKit + Chromium mobile.

Consider also setting overscrollBehaviorY explicitly on the root div for older iOS Safari versions that only honor overscroll-behavior-y — currently 'overscrollBehavior:none' shorthand should cover it, but worth noting if any iOS 15 users report residual bounce.
